page_title: KeyDrift — find API keys leaking in your client bundle

sources.entry: KeyDrift - Scans deployed HTML and JavaScript for exposed secrets while recognizing public browser credentials that should not be treated as leaks.

summary.name: KeyDrift
summary.one_liner: KeyDrift scans a deployed site's client-side JavaScript bundles for API keys and secrets (such as Supabase service_role, Stripe, OpenAI and AWS keys) that were accidentally shipped to browsers.
keywords: devtools search for sk_ or eyj
use_cases: Check a deployed Next.js or Vite app for secret keys shipped in its JavaScript
Find a Supabase service_role key exposed to browsers
Verify that NEXT_PUBLIC_ or VITE_ variables do not leak private credentials
Audit an app built with Lovable, Bolt, Cursor, Replit or v0 for client-side keys
Set up continuous monitoring of client bundle secrets after each deploy
summary.what_it_does: KeyDrift fetches the JavaScript a deployed app actually serves, rather than reading the source repository, and checks it for exposed secrets. It has 21 secret detectors and recognises three public credential formats (such as the Supabase anon key and publishable Stripe key) so they are not reported as leaks. Findings carry a masked prefix and fingerprint rather than the full key, and the page states live keys are never stored. The free tier runs a public scan with no account; paid Indie and Team plans add scheduled monitoring with email, Slack or webhook alerts. The page also lists fix guides for several AI app builders.
notable: Scans deployed client-side JavaScript bundles rather than the repository, catching keys inlined by NEXT_PUBLIC_ or VITE_ at build time
Deliberately ignores public keys such as the Supabase anon key and Stripe publishable key, and uses that to flag a JWT as a service_role key
Stores no live keys; findings are masked and fingerprinted
caveats: Paid plans (Indie $29/month, Team $89/month, Growth from $249/month) are needed for continuous monitoring; the free tier is limited to 1 project, daily scans and 40 chunks per scan
Scans are reported as incomplete when the scanner cannot read all script files referenced by the page
Page lists 21 detectors and specific key formats; coverage beyond these is not described
